title: [Navigation API] Inconsistency between spec and tests for navigating methods and detached iframes

labels.name: topic: navigation API
labels.description: Topics directly related to the navigation API

body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

While implementing the navigation methods in Gecko it turned out that some test expectations do not match the specification expectations (if I understood everything correctly :) ).

Take [this](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/6b1b6210cc781a4c5a854ed0ed139f3690e13e4a/navigation-api/navigation-methods/return-value/reload-rejection-order-detached-unserializablestate.html) test as an example: 

The test performs a navigation on a detached iframe. The navigation should fail, and according to the test it should return rejected promises containing the DOM exception.

However, since the iframe is detached, it is not [fully active](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#destroy-a-child-navigable:~:text=Set%20container%27s%20content%20navigable%20to%20null%2E), which means that promises in the iframe's realm [do not run](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#hostenqueuepromisejob:~:text=If%20job%20settings%20is%20not%20null%2C%20then%20check%20if%20we%20can%20run%20script%20with%20job%20settings%2E%20If%20this%20returns%20%22do%20not%20run%22%20then%20return%2E).

Therefore, according to the spec, the mentioned test should time out. However, in Chrome the test [passes](https://wpt.fyi/results/navigation-api/navigation-methods/return-value/reload-rejection-order-detached-unserializablestate.html?label=experimental&label=master&aligned).
